reviewer.id: OpenAI Codex gpt-5.6-sol independent semantic reviewer with maintainer spot-check
reviewer.method: answer-by-answer semantic review against hidden source rubrics

status_meaning.answer_check_pass: the answer semantically satisfies the check
status_meaning.forbidden_assumption_pass: the answer does not violate the forbidden assumption
status_meaning.not_observable: the supplied model input did not make the criterion reviewable

answer_checks.description: Separate product content and policy from reusable runtime and tooling.
Route broad behavior and source navigation to their owning pages.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not infer the public engine boundary from one embedding project's directory layout.

tasks.notes: Ownership split is clear, but it does not route architecture-wide documentation versus source navigation. It also incorrectly assigns generated filenames and BakingContext state to the project.

answer_checks.description: Name the source directories for tools, scripting, frontend, and server work.
Treat baker implementations as source-backed tools instead of inferring a target name.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not guess a universal target name from a project-specific executable.

tasks.notes: Correctly routes tools, frontend, scripting, and server work to source-backed Engine directories.

answer_checks.description: Limit the reusable Engine contract to the transport, methods, bounds, and command lifecycle.
Keep observations, actions, MCP namespaces, and game policy in the embedding project.
Apply loopback-first operation, non-empty remote tokens, plaintext awareness, and shipping exclusion.
Distinguish protocol proof from native client and server-authority validation.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not publish lf_*, tla_*, one project's observation schema, or administrator actions as generic FOnline protocol methods.

tasks.notes: Transport and security are covered. Project-owned MCP naming/game policy is incomplete, and the protocol proof is not distinguished from real-client, server-rejection, and release-artifact evidence.

answer_checks.description: Classify Engine, project, companion, tool-only, and system dependencies before integration.
Use the public role-scoped helper before core libraries consume the dependency.
Treat development copies, package payloads, licenses, hashes, signing, and isolated acceptance as separate release work.
Separate requested, compiled, and initialized states and preserve allocator/ABI ownership.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not append directly to internal FO_*_LIBS lists, use an unpinned dependency, infer runtime availability from headers, or treat a local post-build copy as package acceptance.

tasks.notes: It classifies delivery models rather than dependency owners, omits the BuildCoreLibraries ordering, isolated package acceptance, and requested/compiled/initialized states. It also conflates project package declarations with BuildTools/PackageInterface.json.

answer_checks.description: Explain module initialization as a defined lifecycle rather than arbitrary startup.
Explain that Yield requires async propagation and creates a suspension boundary.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not invent a project-specific module loader or callback order.

tasks.notes: ModuleInit ordering, async propagation, suspension, reacquisition, and cleanup are supported by the excerpts.

answer_checks.description: Route a module by matching namespace and filename and use the Engine formatter wrapper for AngelScript-specific repairs.
Explain source ordering separately from runtime initialization and use value-tested side macros.
Keep mutable globals exceptional and enter dispatcher-owned attributed functions through their owning route.
Classify mechanical, structural, behavioral, and contract changes before selecting proof.
Keep comment language, game vocabulary, generated formats, migrations, and gameplay acceptance with the embedding project.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not copy one game's comment language, migration backlog, generated files, module catalog, or gameplay test commands into the Engine convention.

tasks.notes: The answer omits generated-output discipline, runtime ModuleInit ordering, dispatcher-owned entry routes, small-batch/contract separation, and project-owned migration/gameplay acceptance.

answer_checks.description: Require the native entry cover or an explicit wider cover for entity access.
State that covers do not survive suspension and must be reacquired.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat Game.Lock as a replacement for entity synchronization.

tasks.notes: Correctly explains entry/wider covers, Yield teardown, reacquisition, and revalidation.

answer_checks.description: Describe deterministic parent and child merge order and overlap risk.
Treat renamed or removed prototype IDs as compatibility changes.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not infer prototype type or gameplay meaning from a project folder name.

tasks.notes: Covers deterministic parent precedence and prototype-ID migration consequences.

answer_checks.description: Require explicit positive IDs unique across critter and item placements.
Resolve inventory and container ownership through the correct authored owner IDs.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not rely on textual section order as an execution-order guarantee.

tasks.notes: Positive shared IDs are covered, but the mandatory $Proto directive for every placement is omitted.

answer_checks.description: Choose the focused viewer and retain later Mapper and client validation.
Review scale, facing, clips, roots, and model hierarchy.
Pin particle seed, prewarm, and direction and compare render paths.
Keep focused inspection, Mapper placement, client behavior, and retained provenance as separate evidence layers.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat a focused viewer as an authoring editor or as proof of gameplay behavior.

tasks.notes: Viewer controls are accurate, but later Mapper/client validation, Draw in scene comparison, exact-revision provenance, and process-start evidence are missing.

answer_checks.description: Orient the author among the map browser, controls, workspace, inspector, and history.
Use the SPARK source editor modes and deliberate save/discard path.
Choose the deferred full-window API and wait before quitting.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat Mapper preview as runtime acceptance or hand-edit baked .spk/.efk output.

tasks.notes: Controls and History are omitted; SPARK Adding/Removing and Save/Discard are absent; the one-pending-request screenshot constraint is not stated.

answer_checks.description: Preserve the human save and runtime-validation boundary around authored map changes.
Drive one warmed map at a time through the reusable loop and quit only after the batch.
Select map-only or full-window capture deliberately and validate visual output.
Keep batch policy and downstream artifact processing in the embedding project.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not use Render.NullRenderer for visual capture or treat file existence as pixel evidence.

tasks.notes: It omits the human dirty/History/diff/runtime boundary, Game.RequestQuit after the batch, TGA/extra-loop details, and most project-owned batch/output policy.

answer_checks.description: Select the narrowest owner and add evidence for every crossed runtime or artifact boundary.
Use semantic readiness/required/forbidden markers under one deadline with bounded cleanup and structured evidence.
Keep game fixtures, script registration, filters, content, backends, and acceptance thresholds in the embedding project.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not turn one game's test registry, content ids, accounts, databases, ports, runners, or acceptance thresholds into an Engine API.

tasks.notes: Narrowest-owner selection is mentioned, but crossed-boundary evidence is not. required_markers, forbidden_markers, the common deadline, and project-owned fixtures/assertions/thresholds are missing.

answer_checks.description: Select the debugger or test route from the failing ownership layer.
Enable and attach the AngelScript debugger through its documented endpoint.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not prescribe a private project's launch profile as an Engine default.

answer_checks.description: Choose on-demand steady-state or total startup tracing through a real profiling configuration.
Profile one standalone side and keep its client or server counterpart regular.
Record workload provenance and reject noisy or incomparable attempts.

tasks.notes: It distinguishes the two profiling modes and one-process boundary, but omits single-config handling, workload/warm-up provenance, and at-least-three comparable captures.

answer_checks.description: Use browser console, network, and Wasm evidence before changing engine code.
Separate build, serving, browser, and server transport layers.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not assume a successful cross-build proves browser runtime behavior.

tasks.notes: Correctly separates package, HTTP, browser/Wasm, and WebSocket/server evidence.

answer_checks.description: Audit every commit and changed path between the exact old and new Engine pins.
Review gameplay, updater, and frozen client ABI boundaries independently.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat a submodule pointer update as sufficient review evidence.

tasks.notes: Audits exact old/new pins and independently reviews gameplay compatibility, updater generation, and frozen host/runtime ABI.

answer_checks.description: Compare stable IDs and contract hashes rather than labels or source positions.
Bind reviewed migration, release, compatibility, and owner decisions to the exact change.

tasks.notes: Stable IDs and contract hashes are covered, but the required change_id binding is omitted.

answer_checks.description: Distinguish compilation, process smoke, source capability, and project qualification.
Require versioned runtime, packaging, renderer, network, and updater evidence for release.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not equate one successful local build with maintained release support.

tasks.notes: Project-qualified is not distinguished explicitly, and the release-evidence list omits Networking.

answer_checks.description: Build declared variants, force-bake the selected config, and package only after inputs exist.
Separate Engine packager capabilities from project release policy, secrets, and signing.
Select an implemented compatible output-producing pack and name its artifact.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not claim signing, store acceptance, or installer support from an Engine payload alone.

tasks.notes: Engine/project ownership is separated, but application builds, ForceBakeResources, and MakePackage are absent. Packs are listed without selecting a compatible pack and naming its artifact.

answer_checks.description: Distinguish baking-host substitutions from target-time directives.
Do not mistake command-line log masking for secret storage or complete redaction.
Keep signing secrets on the protected packaging host and out of generated project files.
Revoke and rotate exposed material rather than trusting deletion or history rewriting.

tasks.notes: Resolution, masking limits, and package-host handoff are correct. It omits the explicit warning that rewriting git history does not revoke exposed credentials.

answer_checks.description: Prefer the foreground headless process under a real supervisor and state the detached daemon boundary.
Require runtime initialization and a functional probe rather than process existence alone.
Use graceful platform signals and do not misread the worker drain setting as a total stop timeout.
Roll back a compatible immutable artifact/config/data unit through the same readiness gate.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat a live process, daemon parent exit, open listener, health file containing Starting..., or ShutdownGraceMs as sufficient end-to-end operational evidence.

tasks.notes: Foreground headless is preferred, but the daemon parent-exit-before-child-readiness boundary is not stated. Readiness, graceful stop, and compatible immutable rollback are otherwise covered.

answer_checks.description: Distinguish the durable set and consistency boundary for Memory, JSON, SQLite, and Mongo.
Explain what the pending and committed recovery logs can and cannot recover.
Require a graceful stop and complete backend/oplog capture when no reviewed online method exists.
Restore a compatible release unit in isolation and validate game semantics across a restart.
Keep RPO/RTO and real disaster-recovery drills project-owned and measured.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not treat an Engine recovery oplog, one SQLite file copied from a live WAL database, a successful provider snapshot, or a backend-only restore as complete production recovery evidence.

tasks.notes: The Memory/JSON/SQLite/Mongo durable sets are not enumerated. It also omits the untested-copy-is-only-a-backup-candidate rule and corrective action from DR drill evidence.

answer_checks.description: Separate Engine-owned stages and helpers from values supplied by the embedding game.
Use the generated project-interface order when more than one CMake input source exists.

Use the helper inventory for exact syntax, owner, invocation context, and revision support.

Resolve disagreements through owning source metadata, machine models, generated references, and then handwritten guidance.
Pin an exact Engine commit and compare every generated contract domain before adoption.

forbidden_assumptions.description: Do not infer stable support from symbol reachability, generated inventory presence, one project's usage, or an unpinned Engine branch.

tasks.notes: Reachability, inventory scope, fallback, and revision pinning are covered. The source hierarchy omits handwritten guidance as the fourth and weakest layer.

Route every new low-level source through the checked Essentials source list and core library.
Keep reusable generator machinery in Engine while the embedding project supplies its own inputs.

tasks.notes: It states umbrella order and FO_ESSENTIALS_SOURCE but omits the parameter/split remedy, EssentialsLib dependency point, and exact all-domain disposition gate.

Separate accepted package dimensions and payload effects from project release, secrets, deployment, and signing policy.
Distinguish compilation, process smoke, source capability, and unsupported public combinations.
Use the generated registry for exact Engine refs, remote visibility/state, source readiness, and observed checks.
